newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech AGM approves Unipetrol merger.
newsitem.headline: Czech AGM approves Unipetrol merger.

text.p: Shareholders of Czech petrochemical concern Chemopetrol Group on Thursday approved the merger of its refining operations into state-held Unipetrol a.s., the CTK news agency reported.
In 1995 Chemopetrol, and the country's other main oil refiner Kaucuk Group a.s., hived off their refining operations to form Ceska Rafinerska, which is 51 percent owned by Unipetrol.

Under a proposal from earlier this year, all three must approve the next step of the plan calling for a swap at a ratio of 1.2 of Unipetrol shares for each Kaucuk a.s. share, and 1.1 of its shares for each Chemopetrol a.s. share.

The swap would entail an exchange of 12 shares of Unipetrol, with a nominal value of 100 crowns each, with one Kaucuk share worth a nominal 1,000 crowns. With Chemopetrol it would be 11 shares at a nominal 100 crowns for one 1,000 crown Chemopetrol share.
Chemopetrol officials confirmed to Reuters that the AGM approved the ratio proposed by Unipetrol.
The plan completes a three-way merger joining the companies as one under the Unipetrol title, as part of the government's petrochemical privatisation plan.
Unipetrol shares are still 100 percent held by the Czech government until the merger is complete.
Unipetrol controls fuels distribution company Benzina, as well as the 51 percent of Ceska Rafinerska.
A consortium of Conoco, Agip SpA, and Royal Dutch/Shell took the remaining 49 percent stake in Rafinerska in 1995.
